Experience with the following software or similar: Integrated Library System Ex Libris Alma, Springshare LibApps, email software, calendar applications, MS office, and Google Apps for Education (such as Google docs).
Demonstrated experience assigning, reviewing and following up on the work of others.
Previous library experience, especially with automated systems.
Experience using computer applications, including word processing and strong keyboarding skills.

Under the general supervision of the Circulation & Collection Maintenance Coordinator, Circulation & Collection Maintenance Assistants perform all functions at the Circulation desk using the library's automated circulation system. Circulation & Collection Maintenance Assistants are responsible for making and implementing all decisions necessary to provide full operation of the University Library circulation desks at either McHenry or the Science & Engineering Library, ensuring Library security and patron safety, and troubleshooting equipment and related problems. Circulation & Collection Maintenance Assistants collaborate with other staff members on projects and work needed to further the progress of the circulation & collection maintenance services as well as participate in section-wide committees. All Circulation & Collection Maintenance staff members are expected to adhere to and support the UCSC Principles of Community, which can be found here:
Able to work independently with minimal guidance and as part of a team.
Understanding of the ways that racism, ableism, and sexism appear in work environments; interest in fostering an inclusive environment that supports a sense of belonging.
Demonstrated interpersonal skills including excellent communication, tact, diplomacy, and flexibility to work effectively with staff, faculty, students, and the public.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to complete assignments with attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy.
Ability to establish priorities and manage multiple activities to meet unit, campus and university deadlines.
Ability to perform multiple tasks simultaneously in a fast-paced environment with frequent interruptions and distractions.
Ability to exercise discretion with regard to sensitive information.
Ability to make decisions following standard library policies and past precedents, recognizing an emergency situation and taking action based on agreed upon procedures.
